metadata.title: MC-001: Restriction Enzyme Digestion - NEB Standard Digest
metadata.purpose: Perform a 50 uL analytical/preparative digest using a selected NEB restriction enzyme and matching NEBuffer.
metadata.scope: Training/library SOP draft. Confirm against the current manufacturer protocol, SDS, and local biosafety/EHS rules before bench use.
beforeYouBegin: Use NEBcloner or the enzyme product page to confirm buffer, incubation temperature, methylation sensitivity, star-activity risk, and heat-inactivation option.
Use high-quality DNA free of ethanol, phenol, salts, SDS, or guanidinium carryover.
For double digests, confirm both enzymes have compatible buffer and temperature conditions.
Keep restriction enzymes on ice or a cold block; add enzymes last.

steps.action: Label reaction tubes and keep them on ice during setup.
For a typical 50 uL reaction, combine DNA, 5 uL 10X NEBuffer, nuclease-free water to near-final volume, and required additive if specified.
Add restriction enzyme last. A common starting point is about 1 uL enzyme for 1 ug DNA, but follow enzyme-specific unit recommendations.

steps.criticalNotes: A common starting point is about 1 uL enzyme for 1 ug DNA, but follow enzyme-specific unit recommendations.

steps.action: Mix gently by pipetting and briefly collect liquid by microcentrifugation.
Incubate at the enzyme-specific temperature and time. For cloning-scale digests, use the manufacturer-recommended condition for complete digestion.
If digest will be analyzed directly, add appropriate loading dye/stop solution and load an aliquot on agarose gel.
If digested DNA will be ligated or assembled, remove enzyme by heat inactivation if allowed, column cleanup, gel extraction, or phenol/chloroform cleanup.
For vector preparation, gel-purify the correctly cut backbone when undigested vector or wrong-size products could create background.

Run an agarose gel with undigested DNA control when interpretation matters. Confirm expected band sizes from a plasmid map or in silico digest. For cloning, quantify purified vector and insert after digestion/cleanup. If no cut is observed, check methylation sensitivity, buffer choice, enzyme activity, DNA purity, and site presence.

troubleshooting.cause: Wrong buffer, methylated site, too little enzyme, poor DNA purity.
troubleshooting.solution: Check enzyme page, use fresh buffer, clean DNA, extend incubation within NEB guidance.

troubleshooting.cause: Too much enzyme, wrong buffer, high glycerol, long incubation.
troubleshooting.solution: Keep enzyme volume low, use recommended buffer, avoid overdigestion.

troubleshooting.cause: Partial digest, plasmid conformation, wrong construct map.
troubleshooting.solution: Compare to undigested control and verify sequence/map.
Cleanup digested DNA and confirm compatible phosphorylated ends.

safety: Wear lab coat, gloves, and eye protection. Use sterile technique for bacterial work and follow local BSL-1/BSL-2 rules as applicable.
Handle UV transilluminators, ethidium bromide or alternative DNA stains, hot agar/media, antibiotics, DMSO, X-gal solvents, and competent cells according to local EHS guidance.
Keep enzymes and competent cells cold as specified. Minimize freeze-thaw cycles and return enzymes to -20 deg C promptly.
Use nuclease-free water and clean tubes for DNA assembly reactions. Avoid EDTA, salts, ethanol, phenol, and guanidinium carryover into ligation, assembly, transformation, or sequencing.
Record construct ID, vector/insert map, antibiotic, host strain, reagent lot, incubation program, colony counts, screen results, and final validation method.
